To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cAMP improves the survival of DA neurons in vitro.

the physical process of cell preparation from embryonic VM may result in the death of DA neurons and that the inclusion of 700μM cAMP in all solutions used during cell preparation can improve survival of DA neurons.

1) cAMP included during cell preparation results in improved survival of DA neurons in vitro; 2) the DA neurons in the cAMP-treated cultures are functional; 3) the cAMP effect is mediated by the activation of a protein kinase; and 4) this protein kinase is a member of the cAMP-dependent family of protein kinases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the survival of DA neurons in vitro and in vivo.
the development of new techniques for the transplantation of dopaminergic cells into the brain of animals with Parkinson's disease.
the development of a novel technique for the treatment for Parkinson's Disease, using embryonic dopaminergic neurons as a therapeutic agent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inclusion of cAMP in all cell suspension preparation solutions from explant to final dissociation improves DA neuron survival in vitro.

the inclusion of 700μM cAMP in all solutions from the explant collection to the final cell suspension preparation results in a 90% survival rate of the dopaminergic neurons originally plated, after 5days in vitro.
the inclusion of dibutyryl-cAMP during cell suspension preparation from VM explants improves the survival of the dopaminergic neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of cAMP in the preparation of cell suspensions for neural transplantation can increase the survival of DA neurons.
we have found a way to improve the survival of the DA cells in culture, and that the process of preparing the cells for culture may be a major cause of death of the DA neurons in culture.
the inclusion of 700 μM of dibutyryl-cAMP in all media from collection of the explant to the final dissociation results in an increase in the survival of DA neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell suspension preparation can be improved by the use of cAMP.
the addition of a cAMP analogue to the cell preparation media can increase cell survival and may be a useful addition to neural transplantation procedures.
cell survival in culture is enhanced if the cells are exposed to cAMP during cell dissociation.
